notes.title: DEV DIARY #10: The full digital Escape Tales: The Awakening launches today!
notes.content:
First of all, we’d like to show you a special launch trailer that we’ve prepared. 😏 You might think you know what to expect, but are you sure? 

[previewyoutube=_8-nkNy4oU0;full][/previewyoutube]

The final version of [b]Escape Tales: The Awakening[/b], the digital adaptation of the bestselling card game under the same title, will launch [b]today at 7 pm CEST[/b] with the price of [b]$7.99[/b]! 
However, [b]till November 3rd[/b] you’ll have a chance to purchase it with a special [b]discount of -38%[/b]! Don’t miss this offer, it won’t last forever!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/3a1d45488138d43413d4d950d4d70e95627ae128.png[/img]

As you might remember from the previous posts, the full version of the game will include:
6️⃣ languages - French, Italian, German, Spanish, English, and Polish 🌍
8️⃣ varied locations with unique vibe ✨
2️⃣6️⃣ challenging puzzles to solve 🧩
3️⃣6️⃣ various items to collect (and use) 🧸
9️⃣ endings - each based on your choices throughout the game 🙌

Escape Tales: The Awakening tells a compelling story about loss, redemption, and the ghosts of the past life. [b]Open exploration, multiple endings, an unforgettable puzzle experience[/b], and an [b]engaging narrative[/b] are only a few of the key features that this title provides. Your moral compass will be put into question and the problem-solving skills pushed to the limits. The game’s puzzles and decisions can be challenging at times, so you’ll have [b]no time limit[/b]. Feel free to take as much time as you need to make up your mind and choose the right path.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/653bc084ac01280a9e20b72a18b7eda8eba7ed80.png[/img]

Don’t forget to tell us your thoughts during and after the gameplay - we’d love to know what you think of the certain locations, characters, puzzles, and the whole game in general. 😎 
Feel free to tag us in all your posts on social media - we can’t wait to see you all play and enjoy the story we’re prepared! 😍

[b]We’d also highly appreciate leaving a review on Steam[/b] - this way we will know what you like and what’s worth working on to make the gameplay and whole experience better and more enjoyable for you in the future! 👉

[h2][b]Get ready for an escape room game
that will keep you at the edge of your seat
from the very beginning![/b][/h2]

notes.title: DEV DIARY #9: What can you expect from the digital Escape Tales: The Awakening
notes.content:
The final version of digital Escape Tales: The Awakening will provide not only a deep narrative story and lots of challenging puzzles, but also many various locations that will transport you into different realities. Not to mention a few different endings of the whole game - each based on the choices you make that will make you question your morals and personal beliefs. 

[h1]LANGUAGES[/h1]
💬 As you’ve probably seen on our social media channels, the final version of Escape Tales: The Awakening will provide 6 distinct languages with which you’ll be able to dive deep into the story and feel every aspect of it. Apart from English, you'll be able to play the final version of the game in French, Italian, German, Spanish, and Polish. 💬


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/67eaf998b1e10a1420c7e741e2bd962f2147c71c.jpg[/img]

[h1]LOCATIONS[/h1]
🌍 Up until now you’ve seen only one location provided in the demo available on Steam - The Basement. Do you know that the full version of the game will consist of as many as 8 locations - each with different vibes, objects, animations, and puzzles? Take a look at two more - however, we won’t yet reveal what place they have chronologically in the game or how they’re named. Play the full game to see and feel for yourself, but for now, take a look at them. 🌍


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/665937d7daee3e4816805718838b25539f47e13a.jpg[/img]

[h1]PUZZLES[/h1]
🧩 More locations and languages are not the only amazing features we had hidden for you. One of the most important elements of the game are puzzles that drive the story towards, help you explore locations, and allow you to find interesting items (that later also may be used). In the final version you’ll be able to solve as many as 26 different puzzles! Each location will give you at least two of them - and every one consists of at least two cards (up to seven!). Get ready for challenging your brain and eyes to mutual cooperation. 🧩


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/88035ec37d70466b2b96de8d0e20fdc34e628660.jpg[/img]

[h1]ITEMS [/h1]
🧸 As stated above, throughout the game you’ll come across many different items to hide in the inventory. Some of them will be of use to go further, others will function as a necessary part of the puzzle, and the rest will allow you to explore the location and see for yourself the deep narrative elements so that you could really step into Sam’ shoes, even for a while. On your path you’ll collect almost 40 various items! 🧸


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/7fc92a381486287711e40790edc464bce3cd44ff.jpg[/img]

[h1]ENDINGS[/h1]
🙌 Some endings are happy, some not so much. In this game, you’ll be the only one deciding about it based on the path you take and the choices you make. Prepare yourself to really get in touch with the emotions and different perspectives and question every little step - you’re the writer of Sam’s story! In the final version of the game, there are 9 various endings to the story - be ready to experience every one of them. 🙌


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/caa3558e107f086c49297f1eed195bf9151b5131.jpg[/img]

With that in mind, we hope now you’re waiting even more for the game premiere on October 24, 2024. 🗓️ Mark that date in your calendar and get ready for the last Dev Diary in two weeks. Till the next read! 👋

[i]Bluekey Games Team[/i]

notes.title: DEV DIARY #8: Escape Tales: The Awakening behind the scenes
notes.content:
With the full version of Escape Tales: The Awakening coming soon, we’d like to take you on a trip behind the scenes once more. 🤠 This time, we’re focusing on the technical aspects of the game, as we’ve managed to ask Tomek, our programist, a few questions about his work on the project and various processes. Would you like to know more? 🤔 Have a good read (and take a closer look at the never-before-seen screenshots!) 👀 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/13d1fe399556b7fb798ee22375a2311f588d1c4e.png[/img]

[i][b]What do you do for Escape Tales: The Awakening?[/b][/i]
I am responsible for the entire programming side of the project. 🖥️ From the overall architecture to the implementation of individual mechanics and UI or even to make “this button less red.”

[b][i]What were the beginnings of your work on this title like?[/i][/b]
Intensive. The project got off to a rather nimble start with the concept phase out of the way. 💥 So the vision of the whole thing was shaped in the so-called “wash.” This made it both interesting and flexible. 🧠


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/9fd9fdecce14c88017a2e0b79e59c0108814675e.png[/img]

[b][i]What was the easiest thing for you to do?[/i][/b]
It's a trick question, but I'll choose the implementation of the game rules. 📝 We ported the title directly from its board version, and thanks to the fact that it had quite clearly outlined rules, you could say that it was “enough” to code them. 🎴

[i][b]What took you the most time and gave you the most challenges?[/b][/i]
We try to deliver the title as quickly as possible. What follows from that - we did almost all the work in parallel. 3D models were already being created in the first week before we even knew how specifically they would be used. ✍️ Therefore, I would say that the most difficult part was coordinating the work and making sure that the project was as flexible as possible in terms of its scalability and modifiability so as not to block anyone's work, while leaving room for corrections and fine-tuning. 🧮


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/2be9731a420309d8f9dd09945570efa3a3df4fd6.png[/img]

That’s all for today, folks! With the premiere of the full version of the game closer and closer we’re getting more and more excited with every single week. 🥳 We hope you’ll soon feel it as much as we do! We’re preparing something really special… 😍

notes.title: DEV DIARY #7: The sounds of Escape Tales: The Awakening
notes.content:
Music-wise, we really wanted the main theme for Escape Tales: The Awakening to convey what the protagonist may feel in the story but also incorporate the dark and mysterious feeling of the game. 🎵 For the music you'll hear in further levels while solving puzzles, we took a different approach - to keep it atmospheric and uneasy yet not that engaging.

The gameplay music is not supposed to keep you distracted, yet focused on solving puzzles. 🔐 This was one of the challenges for Adam (our sound designer), as he loves writing catchy, melodic music, yet it wouldn’t work in this case. Adam had to sort of minimize the sound palette but make it meaningful and memorable at the same time.

What's important for us in this project is to make the sound effects feel vintage and kind of lonely. Items you can notice and interact with in each level are supposed to sound as if they were coming from that space. 🔑 They were treated with tools that help you imagine if you actually dropped or moved something in that particular room. 

We wanted you to feel every inch of the particular location you discover with these sounds. 🎶 Sound effects for all the items in the game are supposed to enhance the feeling, that you are collecting tools needed for progressing in the game. Every card is important and their sound assets are there to emphasize that.

To not be groundless, grab a sneak peak of some of the music you can already hear in the demo, and some more. 👀 Let us know what you think of it!

[previewyoutube=pCBB3ja90go;full][/previewyoutube]

Thanks for taking this trip amongst sounds with us. We hope you’re as thrilled as we are to see and hear everything in the final form! 🤩

[i]Bluekey Games Team[/i]


---
PS Each room you’ll find yourself in throughout the game has its own music theme. One of the tracks even has a little musical puzzle in it. Can you guess which one? 🧐

notes.title: DEV DIARY #6: The origins of the original Escape Tales: The Awakening
notes.content:
[b]In this Dev Diary we’re talking with Bartosz Idzikowski, Lock.Me partner, one of the creators of the board game![/b]

[b][i]What did the prototype of Escape Tales: The Awakening look like?[/i][/b]
At the very beginning, we sketched the first prototypes on paper. ✏️ We created a stack of about 150 pieces of paper; therefore, we had many sketches of the locations and objects. Later we scanned all of them and described to the graphic designer what we would like to do with them next. Very little of it was in Excel or Photoshop, as we wanted to make it fully paper from the very beginning and put as much of our effort as possible. 📝 We felt that using the digital tools would be necessary one way or another, but also wanted the basis to be built from our own ideas and imagination.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/bc3a2fa487f2cb5a90e7a4b8349145098bc6597b.png[/img]

[i][b]Did you have a specific plan for the whole game when creating drafts?[/b][/i]
When we were creating the drafts and sketches for Escape Tales: The Awakening, we also had to come up with a particular game system, accurate for the whole product we had in mind. 🧠 It was a big brainstorming process that took us many, many days, but it brought us great effects. We created the storyline, which we set in a framework, and within that framework we placed the puzzles. 🧮

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/4757287f05053a2e2d3f6faffc0f3b1e7973204a.png[/img]

[i][b]How did you come up with the idea for the story?[/b][/i]
We knew from the beginning that we wanted our games to deal with difficult topics. We were tired of bland plots in escape room games that were just an excuse to solve puzzles. One of our goals was also to have no time limit on gameplay, which allowed us to present a deeper and more complex story. 🧔🙋‍♀️ The story of Sam and Lizzy was an idea born during brainstorming, which we decided to develop further. This idea turned out to be so capacious that we felt from the beginning that this was the right direction and we would succeed in creating an interesting, difficult, but also mysterious story that would move others. 🫂 I think the best “review” is the fact that there were situations where people gave up in the middle of the game with tears in their eyes due to too much emotional weight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/bd896db648ae70a217cd72c2d77be75786c8f46d.png[/img]

[b][i]Did you invent all the puzzles yourselves or were you inspired by something?[/i][/b]
The process of creating puzzles is quite complex. We went over some of them in our heads for a long time until they finally found their place in the game. 🧩 Some of them are inspired by elements found in rooms or moments in the storyline. Sometimes, when we run out of ideas, we make use of known puzzle mechanics - but we always add something ourselves. 💡 However, there is no recipe for coming up with a puzzle. There is, however, a rule - you have to start designing every puzzle with what you want the solution to be.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/c575c9dbaa258ac77ee7446cbb958e464bbdfacb.png[/img]

[b][i]What was the hardest part in creating the whole game?[/i][/b]
The hardest part is always the game testing. Our games are extremely long, which means that a single test took about 4-5 hours. 🕟 On top of that, you have to add time to collect feedback, make adjustments, and update the prototype. These games are one-offs, so the process of finding teams for testing is also quite complex. 👥 During the course of the game's production, dozens of such tests need to be performed, and this creates quite a burden.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/cd930874453139d451da89a95409e8907e9dc62e.png[/img]

[b][i]Which part was the easiest to make and why?[/i][/b]
The puzzles themselves were the easiest to come up with. 🔎 Since this was our first game, we had our heads full of ideas, and the creative process gave a lot of pleasure. Even though it was one of the most time-consuming parts. 🗃️


If you haven’t yet had a chance to play the physical version of Escape Tales: The Awakening, we hope that now you’re even more motivated to try it out - it’s really worth the play! 😄
Until we meet again! 

[i]Bluekey Games Team[/i]

[b]NOTE: All the sketches used in this article are taken from the private collection of Bartosz Idzikowski.[/b]

notes.title: DEV DIARY #5: Graphics and illustrations in Escape Tales: The Awakening
notes.content:
We’ve talked a little bit about the aesthetic vision while creating the demo in the Dev Diary #3, but today [b]we’d like to fully focus on creating the images, graphics, and illustrations[/b] - basically every smaller and bigger detail that your eyes can enjoy while playing the game! 🥰
The game Escape Tales: The Awakening can be divided into two parts:

[b][list]
[*] Narrative
[*] Gameplay
[/list][/b]
[b]Although these elements are closely intertwined, their roles regarding the player are somewhat different.[/b] The first part introduces us to the story, provides context for the entire gameplay, and highlights the protagonist's motivations and fears. It tells the story of a father’s relationship with his daughter, his desperate attempts to save his child, and his longing for lost loved ones. 💔
To effectively convey these elements, [b]we decided to enhance the text[/b] (adapted from the paragraphs in the paper version),[b] with dedicated illustrations displayed simultaneously[/b] with the progression of the story’s paragraphs. 🖼️

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/80ecb32e7bbef67ba3ed2ada5a284faa7ce2e1c5.jpg[/img]

[h1]Narrative[/h1]
The entire narrative [b]takes the form of a sequential picture story[/b] (similar to a comic book), where individual frames capture the essence of the displayed text. [b]The illustrations are divided into three[/b] [b]separate parts:

[list]
[*] Intro
[*] Visions
[*] Outro
[/list][/b]
To accurately capture the essence contained in the paragraphs, [b]we divided the work on the illustrations into three smaller parts: sketching, applying color, and animating[/b] the final illustration (parallax). 📝 [b]The first stage is crucial for selecting the appropriate theme and framing[/b] - the key decisions related to the most important components of the image are made here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/121df226cabdf8838a88731dd32b086644cd8085.jpg[/img]

The second stage, [b]applying color, gives the piece its final form, essentially embedding it with emotions.[/b] 🎨 Importantly, [b]the color palette is based on a pre-prepared script[/b], ensuring that the [b]images are interconnected and that each color used is intentional.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/8b90fcf5e7d0c0c2532b2f10857634ba961b1311.jpg[/img]

[b]Animating[/b] the final illustration [b]is intended to bring the entire piece to life.[/b] Since we are using a digital medium, we strive to take advantage of its benefits wherever possible. 🖥️

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/291497c5b0f31b21c8ab2c450aeb7b39b0885ad6.gif[/img]

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
When constructing the visual layer of the gameplay, [b]we aimed to maintain as much consistency with the paper version as possible[/b], to ensure that the original gameplay experience was not disrupted or altered. 🎴 [b]However, this did not mean a direct 1:1 transfer - where possible, we introduced enhancements.[/b] Cards, depending on their category, received a uniform background and animation ([b]parallax[/b], similar to the illustrations).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/e6fb960cbd79906c3df31cedc805639e538eefc6.gif[/img]

[b]Choice cards were moved to the narrative section[/b], with the selection itself integrated into the text layer. 📖 This approach helps [b]to streamline the gameplay and creatively leverage the digital platform.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/65ba649177fae7988fc17758fe5d8e73feaae4f5.jpg[/img]

[b]Visions were given a separate screen - this is a unique moment in the game that deserves its own visual treatment.[/b] Here, players learn about the character's history, what has happened in their past, and make important gameplay decisions. 🔥 To emphasize the uniqueness and surreal nature of this gameplay moment,[b] the entire scene was given a blood-red color palette.[/b]
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/eb8b4d13d6a5bf720cffe7ab9d5bcf47c5d3bfc0.jpg[/img]

In summary, when developing the visual layer of Escape Tales: The Awakening, we aimed to stay as true as possible to the original, paper version of the game. 🎲 However, where possible, given the digital format and the opportunities it offers, we introduced enhancements that increase player immersion and improve the fluidity and enjoyment of the gameplay. 🎮


---
Now we’re all on the same page with the whole graphic process that’s happening in Escape Tales: The Awakening - cool, isn’t it? 😃  [b]We can’t wait to show you what we prepared for the next time in two weeks - see you then! [/b]

notes.title: DEV DIARY #4: How the still became animated in Escape Tales: The Awakening
notes.content:
Three weeks after the demo’s premiere, we’re bringing you the fourth part of our Dev Diary. [b]Did you already have a chance to try out the demo?[/b] 😏 If yes, feel free to let us know on social media or write us a private message - [b]we appreciate all the feedback! [/b]🤗

Without further ado, [b]let’s dive into the world of animation…[/b]

The process of creating animations for the digital version of Escape Tales: The Awakening can be divided into several distinct, but closely related, categories, including:
[list]
[b][*] GUI and text animations
[*] Location asset animations
[*] Decorative animations[/b]
[/list]Each of the above categories involves different aspects and functions that the animations serve. In the case of [b]GUI (Game User Interface) animations, the primary focus is on ensuring the intuitive and smooth interactions[/b] during the game. 🎮 [b]Animations related to assets highlight interactive areas for the player[/b], corresponding to previously performed actions. [b]Decorative animations, on the other hand, serve an aesthetic purpose[/b], enhancing the overall visual level of the game. 🧸

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/cfa3758bc617eaddf29f8985d541785a6e19bccf.gif[/img]


[h1]GUI Animations[/h1]
As mentioned above, animations related to this category are primarily functional. For instance, they indicate whether and how a given button or text is interactive. 🕹️ [b]Typically, they are based on the basic visual properties of the object, such as its color, size, or rotation.[/b] This is not done randomly, as the animation layer is meant [b]to support the user experience[/b] rather than distract from it. 🔴

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/0fb04abe44420fe943b15faaed2491481cf0ca72.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/b143e96a2646aab9fe9e13ad2baa8f972bec0bd1.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/0a1e96e92171d174629c9d1c0e48372b50e97edf.gif[/img]


[h1]Location Asset Animations[/h1]
Similar to the above, these are partially functional animations. [b]They indicate the place (or places) where a specific interaction has occurred.[/b] However, since they are placed in the game world, i.e., in a given location, [b]the visual layer plays a slightly more significant role here than in the first category[/b] - some animations contain extended visual features. 🖼️ The movement paths of some objects are smoothed, sometimes enriched with particles (VFX) or appropriate lighting. This is a natural step related to the expansion of the platform on which the game takes place. In the case of the paper version, all described interactions with objects remain in the player's imagination. 🧠 In the digital world, however, there is an excellent opportunity to use them to enhance the visual quality of the entire game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/1c0e9abf653d9ccba2db8654ac38f021ad6fca97.gif[/img]


[h1]Decorative Animations[/h1]
The last category [b]serves a purely aesthetic function[/b]. It is not an essential element for gameplay, but [b]it has a significant impact on the user's immersion and visual perception[/b]. 👀 Animated elements are placed peripherally in relation to the gameplay area; they do not directly correlate with it but excellently emphasize the character of a given location. [b]For example, in the case of a basement, small spiders move across the screen[/b] - some weave webs or shake on them in a manner characteristic of these insects. 🕸️

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/06b8a30af0298f0de2e6fe3830bb3c1a817ef2b3.gif[/img]

---
We hope that now the distinction of various animations in Escape Tales: The Awakening is clear for you and you see what the full process looked like behind the scenes! 🤠 [b]From now on, you’ll surely notice more and more details while playing the demo - and the full version in the future![/b] 
[b]Thanks for taking this trip with us and until we meet again! [/b]👉

[i]Bluekey Games Team[/i]



---
PS. In the meantime, don’t forget to [b]Add the game to your [i]Wishlist[/i][/b] and [b][i]Follow[/i][/b] it to stay up to date. 😏

notes.title: DEV DIARY #3: The making of Escape Tales: The Awakening DEMO
notes.content:
Due to the fact that creating the demo was a complex project, we'd like to present to you the whole process from a few different perspectives - the software, the graphics, and the sounds.

[h1]🧩 First, there was a code…[/h1]
At the very beginning, without making any decisions or assumptions, our team played the board version of the game. 🎴 Then, they played the digital version available on Tabletopia to identify any issues with the digital adaptation compared to the board game. Based on these observations, the team created an initial sketch of their goals, forming a preliminary vision of the final game. 📝

The team focused primarily on preserving and enhancing the features that players loved in the original version. At the same time, they aimed to address and level out the features players complained about. 🖼️ Additionally, they sought to enrich the overall experience by leveraging the advantages of the digital format, such as improved graphics, music, and a game-saving system. 

A prototype was then created as the foundation for a future demo. Deep within the code, the team maintained the concept of a paragraph card game, allowing for straightforward modifications to the gameplay logic. 🎮 On top of this foundation, they added enhanced graphics and other improvements unique to the digital version, such as the ability to note something on the screen while solving puzzles, automate paragraph searches, or automate various actions such as taking a card or putting down tokens. 🪙 The prototype underwent numerous iterations, tests, and adjustments, ultimately culminating in the creation of the demo.

Importantly, from the beginning, the team was guided by the concept of creating a content editor rather than a closed game. Initially, they developed general mechanisms, such as an inventory system and a puzzle-solving panel, which were then adapted to handle varied content. 🕹️ Once this system was functional, the team used it as the foundation to build the demo.

[h1]🧩 What about the aesthetic vision?[/h1]
The process of preparing the demo from an artistic perspective included several sequential stages. 🎨 The first was the development of concept art, which allowed for determining the proportions, layout, and character of all essential gameplay elements, such as:
[list]
[*] text field
[*] location section
[*] collected equipment, also known as “Inventory”
[/list]
During this stage, the idea came up to convert flat locations from cards into a 3D model. 🃏 This made the visuals more attractive and made it easier to manage things like adding animations to individual assets.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/3d5d962e67d886714f22078bcfb8f47c3710b4fb.png[/img]
[i]Illustration 01. One of the first concept artworks.[/i]

At this time, the chosen font (inspired by old typewriters) was decided on, and the artistic style of the user interface was developed. 📇


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/22bb139117854b6b85d01c78140a27cf2a9c085e.png[/img]
[i]Illustration 02. Font (inspired by old typewriters).[/i]

Next, the idea of using old Polaroid photos as inventory assets also emerged. 📸


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/9cb81c628f554ba12a1bc8dc4510355a2e9a5f16.png[/img]
[i]Illustration 03. An old Polaroid style used for an inventory asset.[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/59551346b8b93d86c74be489a09a8640ffbc779a.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/8b13af48729138b25376bdc77c78957a26c502f4.png[/img]
[i]Illustration 04 and 04a. GUI (Game User Interface) elements.[/i]


Importantly, each of the above elements was continuously consulted from a technical standpoint (implementation feasibility) and user experience (UX).

After the conceptual phase was completed, it was time for the actual production work. 💻 To maintain both visual and gameplay consistency, lists were developed to clearly define the frameworks for the subsequent stages of implementation:
[list]
[*] List of all necessary graphic elements
[*] List of narrative illustrations
[*] List of all animations (both GUI and decorative, including text animations)
[*] List of visual effects (VFX)
[/list]
Simultaneously, initial tests of using shaders on 3D locations began. 🖌️ The goal was to closely replicate the visual style of the paper version (which was undoubtedly achieved) while retaining all the advantages and flexibility of the implemented 3D model.
 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/483d73c09b86547f672dc596bb417a0592d9d94b.png[/img]
[i]Illustration 05. Three-dimensional model of the first location with applied shader.[/i]


Summarily, step by step, list by list, additional components of the project emerged. Naturally, not everything could be implemented exactly as conceived initially. 🧮 However, the final demo version maintains a very high level of visual consistency with the initial artistic frameworks and the paper prototype. 

The demo serves as an excellent platform for continuing the project, with opportunities to adjust and improve individual elements (which is an ongoing process). 📈 Considering the target platform, we continuously evaluate gameplay enhancements (such as VFX and animations), which breathe more life and flair into the paper-inspired version while retaining all its advantages. 

[h1]🧩 How does the mystery sound like?[/h1]
Music-wise, we really wanted the main theme for Escape Tales: The Awakening to convey what the protagonist may feel in the story but also incorporate the dark and mysterious feeling of the game. 🎵 For the music you'll hear in further levels while solving puzzles, we took a different approach - to keep it atmospheric and uneasy yet not that engaging.

When it comes to sounds, what's important for us in this project is to make the sound effects feel vintage and kind of lonely. Items you can notice and interact with in each level are supposed to sound as if they were coming from that space. 🔑 They were treated with tools that help you imagine if you actually dropped or moved something in that particular room. We wanted you to feel every inch of the particular location you discover with these sounds. 🎶



That’s all for today, folks! We hope you had a blasting time with us - till the next time! 🤠

[i]Bluekey Games Team[/i]



---

[h1][b]If you haven’t played the demo yet - give it a try![/b][/h1] We promise it’s gonna be an unforgettable experience! 😎

---
PS. In the meantime, don’t forget to [b]Add the game to your [i]Wishlist[/i][/b] and [b][i]Follow[/i][/b] it to stay up to date. 😏

notes.title: DEV DIARY #2: All you need to know about the inventory cards
notes.content:
[h2]🃏 What are the inventory cards?[/h2]
Depending on the location, the player's task is to [b]collect equipment, i.e., items necessary for solving puzzles[/b] (e.g., finding a key to unlock a padlock). These items, once selected with the cursor, are placed in the inventory. They [b]can be used or even combined to e.g. explore the location or create new objects[/b]; it all depends on their original purpose and the related symbols. Some of the cards will show a closer perspective of a certain location or object so that it’ll be easier to solve the puzzle, seeing all the details included in this particular area or thing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/9961be140c1caf7ebe97f649451a2d135a3993d9.png[/img]

[h2]🃏 What cards might actually appear in the game?[/h2]
In the digital version of the game, the [b]items take the form of old Polaroids[/b], with a visual representation of each item as a photograph. This supports the narrative of the entire game, enhances the overall visual reception, and makes managing resources easier. 📸
In the first location (which can be seen in the teaser trailer and in the first dev diary), there will be cards connected strongly with the basement, in which the player starts the game as the main character. While exploring this location, players might encounter objects such as tools, chalk, and candles. Why? We can’t tell. You will see when the time comes… 😏

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/b5c7a24a25351b3086fb739c2212318fc798506e.png[/img]

[h2]🃏 How should I read the cards?[/h2]
[b]To increase readability, where possible, items were placed on a uniform background[/b], allowing the content of a given card to be quickly read. This does not overwhelm the players, but rather allows them to focus all their energy on… solving puzzles and enjoying the gameplay. 🧩
[b]The symbols on the cards[/b] were directly taken from the paper version of the game, but they have gained a new attribute: they [b]become highlighted if there is a dependency between the cards in the inventory[/b]. This should provide the player with a more readable and comfortable experience while interacting with the inventory. 🔦

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/1c036ea1bfcb7bc27eaba39af432a031cee3fd94.png[/img]

[h2]🃏 How did we transform the paper cards into digital ones?[/h2]
[b]Animations related to displaying the cards were designed to emphasize the fluidity of the entire gameplay[/b] - photos appear, disappear, and change their position smoothly, pleasing to the eye. There are no unnecessary special effects here, so as not to distract the player from the game area. 😌
All these processes contribute to a visually pleasing and comfortable inventory for gameplay, which is not only an important visual element of the screen, but also an essential element for gameplay. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/c7b0d1f5059ad46964d19d30900f02e6577e21ca.png[/img]


Thanks for taking this trip among the cards with us! [b]Hopefully now you feel more engaged in the gameplay and prepared for the surprise that will be revealed next week… 👀 Stay tuned for more info![/b]

[I]Bluekey Games Team[/i]


PS
In the meantime, don’t forget to [b]Add the game to your [i]Wishlist[/i][/b] and [i][b]Follow[/b][/i] it to stay up to date. 😏

notes.title: DEV DIARY #1: The beginnings of digital Escape Tales: The Awakening
notes.content:
We’re really happy to see that you’re satisfied with the [b]teaser trailer[/b] and waiting for more. In case some of you haven’t seen it, [b]take a look[/b]:

[previewyoutube=nVTeZK6mRwU;full][/previewyoutube]
There's been a lot going on in the studio since we started the works and we’ve decided to share with you some behind the scenes so that you could see how we bring to life your beloved card [b]game created by LockMe and Board&Dice![/b] 🤗 In the first Dev Diary we’d like to focus on the process of  that you would see in the final product. 


[h2]How did it all start? 🤔 [/h2]

🃏 At the very beginning, our graphics team had carefully studied the location cards in order to be able to put it 1:1 from the physical version of the game to the digital one. Both location cards were joined to create the whole basement and the sections were divided into squares to see what elements fit which space. Then, the whole location looked like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/47a3eaee033616fb529428bd69f3fa05f3427e99.png[/img]
🃏 Later, the standard version of the location cards was exported and the team prepared the whole location so that it would not include the interactive elements. Next, all of these elements were separated from the location to bring it as a whole to the digital dimension. Square by square, the graphics team paid attention to every detail to transfer all the interactive elements visible on the location cards, such as the safe, tools or chest. 🛠️ They separated the elements from the basement location and transferred it to the digital realm.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/a73173c6e75921594c8012178419ee25cd851358.png[/img]


[h2]Why the fisheye perspective? 👁️[/h2]
🐟 In the paper version of the game, the location is shown with two cards, each showing half of the room. To see the whole room, you have to line up the bottom edges of these cards. This can look a bit strange because one half of the picture is flipped upside down, which can make it hard to understand the room's shape, where things are, or what you need to do in the game based on the pictures. 🚪

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/5d57e72f824dc1cdf806546e7fcbf9f6d49553eb.png[/img]
🐟 To fix this problem, our team used a fisheye perspective, which makes the whole room look balanced and unified, no matter where objects are. This gives the player the feeling of looking down at the room from above, making it easy to see everything clearly, even the walls that are at different angles. 

🐟 Also, changing straight lines into curved ones makes the picture look softer and easier on the eyes. This helps the player’s eyes move smoothly over the image without hitting any sharp edges. It makes the game feel more smooth and flexible. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/db4eaf9aef071a7833bb8d9f3110bcecf0109eeb.png[/img]
🐟 Since this perspective doesn't happen naturally and is made by bending light in a special way, it looks unique and interesting. This makes the picture (and the game) more memorable and less ordinary. 🧠

🐟 Labeling objects is also important with the fisheye perspective. Since it looks like a camera lens effect, the labels get distorted too.  The final effect can be seen below:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048887/4951d097fbcb4e28954ced972f38b61218e01f48.gif[/img]

[h2]And for the final part...[/h2]
We’ve prepared for you a little [b]fun fact[/b]: 
😎 The [b]height of the camera above the room is of no small importance[/b] here - the lower it is, the more pronounced and surreal the curves become. 😎

We hope that this piece of info will introduce you better to the digital world of Escape Tales: The Awakening. 😃 Stay tuned for more info and the [b]next part of the Dev Diary coming in two weeks![/b] 😍

[i]Bluekey Games Team[/i]
